articles.title: Benhard Janse van Rensburg knew nothing of potential South Africa call-up
articles.summary: Centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg admits he "probably would have loved to" play for his native South Africa, but denies Rassie Erasmus' claims he was in talks over a Springboks call-up.
articles.body:
Centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has admitted that he "probably would have loved to" play for his native South Africa, but denied Rassie Erasmus' claim he was in talks over a Springboks call-up before making his England debut.

Janse van Rensburg, who represented South Africa's under-20 side, became eligible for England this summer after living in the country for five years and scored on his Test bow against Fiji in Liverpool in July.

The previous week South Africa head coach Erasmus had claimed Van Rensburg had been "very keen" in talks with Springboks officials, but ultimately wasn't selected.

"I only heard about it because my dad told me Rassie said it," Janse van Rensburg told Rugby Union Weekly.

"I would have probably loved to, but really every team I play for, I want to do my best and whatever comes after that, comes after that.

"When Rassie said he wanted to pick me, I was in the dark.

"I hadn't heard anything from them. Whatever he said, whether that was true or not, I didn't know about it."

Rugby Union Weekly: Janse van Rensburg, Itoje and Russell join the pod

The selection of the 29-year-old for England ahead of talents brought through the domestic system has attracted criticism.

Danny Care, who won 101 caps in his England career, said Janse van Rensburg's selection "doesn't sit right", while former centres Jeremy Guscott , external and Mike Tindall , external also questioned the call.

Janse van Rensburg has tried to avoid the commentary around his promotion into the England team, but says he can see its critics' perspective.

"It is understandable that that there's going to be some people that don't like it and some people that do like it," he added.

"People probably still have their thoughts and how they feel about it.

"For me, I probably can't prove them wrong. I just want to do my best for whichever team I play for.

"It's an honour and a privilege to go to that next level of playing rugby."

Janse van Rensburg crossed for a try three minutes after coming on for Henry Slade in the 73-8 win over Fiji, before also appearing off the bench in the 31-24 win in Argentina the following weekend.

He says his integration has been eased by having previously played the Call of Duty video game against some of the squad, with a Leicester group including Jack van Poortvliet, George Martin and Freddie Steward joining him online.

While on tour this summer, he has been successful in more analogue pursuits.

"I think I made about 300-odd pounds on tour, just by winning all the cards," he said

"At Bristol we play, but not for money, so I've just gotten good at it. And then, as soon as it was for money, I just pocketed.

"All of the boys have just made me feel like I'm playing a normal game for my local club. They made me feel so welcome and it is so easy for me to not have any nerves and just go and enjoy it."

articles.title: Super League: Bradford Bulls 32-22 Castleford Tigers - bottom side end losing run
articles.summary: Bradford Bulls end a seven-match losing streak with victory over troubled Castleford Tigers in the struggle to avoid the Super League wooden spoon.
articles.body:
Tries: Dean, Wynne, Aekins, Russell, Blake, Scurr Goals: Atkin 4

Tries: Senior, Mpapalangi 2, A Mellor Goals: Weaver 3

Bradford Bulls ended their run of seven straight defeats and deepened the gloom surrounding Castleford Tigers at Odsal Stadium.

The return of three experienced forwards gave Bradford a major boost as they dominated from the start against Castleford, who are without a head coach and have now lost six of their past seven games since beating league leaders Leeds Rhinos in July.

Bottom-of-the-table Bradford took control by half-time with tries from Riley Dean, Connor Wynne, Caleb Aekins, Dan Russell and Waqa Blake as scrum-half Chris Atkin ran the show, while Louis Senior's try was Castleford's only score of the first half.

They improved in the second half with two tries from Krystian Mapapalangi and one from Alex Mellor, but Ebon Scurr's try 12 minutes after the interval was enough to keep Castleford at arm's length and move the Bulls level on points with York Knights, Huddersfield Giants and Hull FC with one game to play.

Bradford are intent on avoiding the wooden spoon in their first season back in Super League and they have given themselves a chance, especially as they face second-bottom York Knights in the final game next Thursday.

They were still a player short of naming a 21-man squad but the return of Ryan Sutton, Dan Russell and Phoenix Steinwede added punch to the pack, while Atkin was out to prove a point against his former club.

Joe Mellor sent Dean over for an early opener and Castleford were in defensive disarray as Wynne benefited from Atkin's floated pass before Aekins hacked a loose ball forward and won the race to touch it down under the posts.

Mapapalangi was a bright spot for Castleford and he sent Senior over for a try, but the ubiquitous Atkin set up both Russell and Blake for tries to end the contest by half-time.

Castleford managed to get on the front foot after the break and Mapapalangi, now over his shoulder injury, introduced an element of doubt with an early try.

Scurr was central to Bradford's forward dominance and he was rewarded with his first Super League try before Castleford's Alex Mellor forced his way over at the other end. Mapapalangi scored his second a minute before the final hooter to add some respectability to the scoreline.

Bradford coach Kurt Haggerty told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I'm really pleased with how we defended. We conceded a couple of tries off kicks which in this weather is probably the only way you are going to break teams down, but we showed resilience defensively and still managed to score some pretty special tries.

"We thought we should have got the game won over in Toulouse, so we carried the momentum over and kept our week really positive leading into this game.

"Riley [Dean] and Chris Atkin have played some games back-to-back together now and it showed. Riley was really good tonight and Chris got us around the field, a lot came through those two, but you have to give credit to our back field who carried the ball really strongly."

Castleford interim coach Luke Robinson told BBC Radio Leeds:

"We're a side that's severely lacking confidence. If we don't start well, then all of a sudden everything seems to fall apart and we don't seem to be able to have the resilience to stay in it.

"We made 30 tackles more than them before the 20-minute mark, so all you are doing is depleting yourself of energy and giving the other side a leg-up.

"The analysts told me after the game that we average 34 points a game conceded, which is a crazy stat that shows where we need to be at. The best sides are the ones that defend, and we've got to find that."

Bradford: Aekins; Okunbor, Russell, Blake, Wynne; Dean, Atkin; Sutton, Ackers, Scurr, Gardiner, Steinwede, J. Mellor.

Interchanges: Gill, Peposho, Ruan, Hooley.

Castleford: Laulu-Togagae; Ravalawa, A. Mellor, Mapapalangi, Senior; Asi, Weaver; Dupree, Hood, Lawler, Lane, Greacen, Stimson.

Interchanges: Hall, Brown, Vaalepu, McNamara.

articles.title: Beno Obano: Bath prop to move to Pau and put England career on ice
articles.summary: Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice after agreeing to join French side Pau at the end of the forthcoming season.
articles.body:
Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice with a move to France, after agreeing to join Top 14 side Pau from Bath at the end of the forthcoming season.

The 31-year-old loose-head prop won his fifth cap in the defeat by South Africa in July, backing up first-choice Ellis Genge off the bench.

Head coach Steve Borthwick is restricted to a domestic-based talent pool as a key part of the relationship between Prem clubs and the Rugby Football Union over elite players.

England are relatively well stocked at loose-head, with Harlequins' Fin Baxter, Northampton's Emmanuel Iyogun and Sale's Bevan Rodd all younger than Obano and vying for a role.

Sale's versatile 22-year-old Asher Opoku-Fordjour can also pack down on that side of the front row.

It is unlikely England will rule out selecting Obano this season, as they did when Tom Willis announced in October that he would move to Bordeaux-Begles for 2026-27.

Despite starting three matches in the 2025 Six Nations, impressing in a summer series win over Argentina and being awarded a central contract for the year, Willis was exiled from the squad, with Borthwick instead focusing on players who would be available for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Obano, who isn't on a central contract, will be available for the tournament, just as David Ribbans and Joe Marchant were when they went into the 2023 edition having agreed moves to France for the following season.

He will join an impressive list of England talent out in France with Jack Willis, Kyle Sinckler, Billy Vunipola, Manu Tuilagi, Lewis Ludlam and Sam Simmonds all currently playing their club rugby across the Channel and outside England eligibility.

Obano's departure will cause Bath more front-row upheaval. South African powerhouse Thomas du Toit left for the Durban-based Sharks at the end of the last campaign, while Scotland international Jamie Bhatti arrived this summer.

articles.title: Noah Caluori: I played with torn wrist ligament for most of last season
articles.summary: Wing sensation Noah Caluori says he played through the pain of a torn wrist ligament during his break-out season for Saracens and England
articles.body:
Teenage wing sensation Noah Caluori has revealed that he spent the majority of his breakthrough season - featuring 18 tries in 13 Prem games and an England debut - playing with a detached ligament in his wrist.

The 19-year-old sustained the injury when he came down heavily on his arm while competing for a high ball in Saracens' defeat by Exeter in December.

After consulting both club and national team coaches, Caluori opted to play through his pain and wait until the summer for an operation to reconnect the ligament.

"It would just hurt," said Caluori. "A lot of movements hurt, I had to modify a lot of my gym plans, catching the high balls hurt.

"I learnt how to manage the pain. That's it, really.

"I came to the conclusion that I'm going to push for this. I'm going to hope that I go on tour [with England], I'm going to try for the best season I can for Saracens, try and help us get to the play-offs.

"You just ride the adrenaline and learn to get on with it."

Caluori posted a picture on social media in July of himself in a hospital bed with a heavily bandaged right wrist.

Explaining now why it felt right to keep playing, he said: "Saracens and England gave me the freedom. If it was too bad and I wasn't able to play, they would have not let me.

"But they gave me the freedom to choose, I chose what I wanted to do, and then you've just got to live with your decision. I was pretty happy that I've done it."

While Saracens fell just short of the Prem play-offs, failing to overhaul Exeter in a final-day shoot-out for a semi-final spot, Caluori succeeded in his other aims.

He finished as the top flight's joint-top try-scorer, made a try-scoring debut for England against Fiji, and then appeared off the bench again in victory over Argentina the following weekend.

Caluori, whose mother Grace is a psychotherapist, regularly lists and revises his goals for the future.

He is determined that his career should not fizzle out, which has happened with some other young prodigies in the past.

"I've had multiple chats with people, and it's just similar things: 'You have the ability to do it, it just matters about your mentality'," said Caluori.

"They've seen loads of players who have done similar to what I've done, then drop off in two or three years because they got complacent.

"I don't think I'm that type of person. I'm very hungry for everything."

Caluori will miss Saracens' Prem opener away to Leicester on Sunday, 27 September as he continues his recovery, but he could be in contention for their home game against Sale seven days later.
